summary: Feed s140_double to APM is degraded: 21.2% one-way TCP sessions and 5.6% packet loss detected. APM requires bidirectional visibility and will have incomplete transaction timing and missing data.

findings.root_cause: 28 of 132 TCP sessions (21.2%) show only one direction, exceeding 10% threshold. Most likely asymmetric routing with packet broker not aggregating both directions to same tool port, or SPAN/TAP only covering one side of the path. Traffic from client->server and server->client is being split or one side is not captured.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM needs_both_directions=true. One-way flows prevent transaction response-time calculation, TCP handshake analysis, and application latency breakdown - APM will report incomplete or failed transactions and miss performance issues.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same APM tool port via packet broker flow-aware aggregation to restore bidirectional visibility required for APM.

findings.root_cause: 96 of 1713 TCP packets (5.6%) show gaps/retransmissions indicating capture loss upstream of tool, exceeding 1% threshold. Tool overload is healthy, so loss is not at APM ingress. Most likely SPAN port buffer exhaustion/oversubscription on source switch or packet broker ingress drops due to burst microbursts.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM will see incomplete flows, retransmission noise, and inaccurate latency/error counts. Even though APM needs_full_payload=false, missing packets break TCP sequence reconstruction and transaction correlation, degrading detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: TAP provides lossless, full-duplex capture without SPAN buffer drops or switch CPU contention, eliminating the 5.6% loss before the packet broker. If TAP not immediately possible, add packet broker buffering/filtering to reduce SPAN oversubscription.
